questions.question: In Spring, what does Inversion of Control mean?
options: The container, not your own code, creates objects and connects them
Your code must call new for every helper it needs
Objects are created in reverse alphabetical order
Controllers run before services start
questions.explanation: Control of object creation and wiring moves from your classes to the Spring container.

questions.question: Which type represents the Spring IoC container?
options: ApplicationContext
CommandLineRunner
SpringBootApplication
ComponentScan
questions.explanation: ApplicationContext is the container that creates beans, injects dependencies and manages their life.

questions.question: LibraryDesk needs FineCalculator, and both are @Component classes that print a line in their constructors. Which line does Spring print first?
options: The line from LibraryDesk, because it is the main class
The line from FineCalculator, because the desk needs it
Both lines at the same moment
Neither, because constructors are skipped
questions.explanation: Spring builds the helper first so it can pass it into the constructor of the class that needs it.

questions.question: A developer writes DeskRunner desk = new DeskRunner(new LibraryDesk(null)); inside another bean. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, this is how IoC is meant to work
Constructors cannot take parameters in Spring
The objects are created by hand, so Spring does not manage them or inject their helpers
The code needs the @Override annotation
questions.explanation: Objects made with new are ordinary objects outside the container, so they get no injection or lifecycle handling.

questions.question: A FineCalculator class has no annotation at all, but LibraryDesk asks for it in its constructor. What happens at startup?
options: Spring creates it silently with default values
The app starts and the calculator is null
Spring reports that it cannot find a bean of that type and stops
Spring scans other packages until it finds one
questions.explanation: Without @Component or another bean definition, the container has no bean to inject, so startup fails.
